content: Each task performed in the datasets is designed to assess different cognitive functions, e.g. fluency task is used to evaluate the ability to organize and plan BIBREF18 and picture description task – for detecting discourse-related impairments BIBREF19 . As a result, it is expected that the nature of decision functions and feature predicates learned on data of each of these tasks would be different. Performance of AD identification with addition of normative data from multiple tasks (Tab. SECREF7 ), despite the possibly different nature of decision functions, suggests that training the model with samples from each task provides domain-specific inductive bias for other tasks. We study possible underlying mechanisms responsible for this, suggested by Caruana et al. BIBREF20 and Ruder et al. BIBREF21 .
